newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCH HALTED BY PITCH INVASION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCH HALTED BY PITCH INVASION.

text.p: A pitch invasion halted the Brighton-Lincoln third divison game on Tuesday -- hours after the English League refused a postponement request by fans fearing trouble.
About 50 Brighton followers charged on to the pitch after Lincoln went ahead in the 25th minute. Referee Steve Bennett took the teams to the safety of the dressing-rooms.
The group of supporters then sat in the centre circle and were joined by another 100 fans from other parts of the ground.
After a seven-minute protest they returned peacefully to the stands and play resumed five minutes later.
The invasion happened despite an increased police presence but trouble had been forecast by Brighton Supporters' Club vice-chairman Liz Costa.
Fans are incensed about Brighton's 94-year-old Goldstone ground being sold off to property developers and the club possibly folding or moving to another town.
Costa had said earlier: "I think we ought to try and get this game called off. The crowd trouble could be so serious tonight that I think it's better to call it off earlier in the day."
Brighton, 1983 F.A. Cup finalists, are nearly bottom of the lowest division.
There was serious trouble at the ground last season and a match against York was abandoned when fans swarmed on to the pitch and smashed the goalposts.
